message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | Key Points | |------|--------------|------------| | **1. Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | • If the first card is an action card, its effect applies to the first player. | | **2. Turn Order** | • Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a “Reverse” card is played). | • The direction can change mid‑game. | | **3. Playing a Card** | • On your turn, play one card that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. | • You may play a card from the drawn card if it’s playable. | | **4. Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two (+2)** – next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn. | • Wild Draw Four can only be played if you have no other playable card (otherwise you can be challenged). | | **5. Winning a Turn** | • After playing a card, if you have no cards left, you win that round. | • You must shout “UNO!” when you have one card left. | | **6. Scoring** | • The round ends when a player discards all their cards.
• The winner scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards remaining in opponents’ hands:
 – Number cards: face value.
 – Skip, Reverse, Draw Two: 20 points each.
 – Wild, Wild Draw Four: 50 points each. | • First player to reach 500 points (or another agreed total) wins the game. | | **7. Optional House Rules** | • **Stacking** – players may stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing.
• **No Challenge** – Wild Draw Four can be played anytime.
• **Custom Decks** – add extra action cards or themed decks. | • Agree on house rules before starting. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep an eye on colors** – try to keep a variety so you’re not stuck with one color. 2. **Use Wild cards strategically** – save them for when you’re about to win or to force opponents into a tough spot. 3. **Watch opponents’ cards** – if they’re low on cards, they might be holding a Wild Draw Four. 4. **UNO shout** – remember to say “UNO!” when you have one card left; otherwise you’ll have to draw two penalty cards. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
